_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.
orderSource: the Handbook ranking control (scripts/handbook-shell.html), saved by Mike on 2026-08-15. It replaced design/mockups/to-do-list-table.html, which set the order before it.

items.name: The 21 branches that still name a page nobody can open
items.why: Of the 55 recommendations across the logic tables, 28 lose text to the template gate because they name a page that does not exist in the 291-record library. Seven were the Get Seminar branches, fixed 2026-08-15 once Mike named the real page (Design & Deliver). The other 21 sit in the fmc_, cas_, fbp_ and ol_ tables and nobody has looked at them.
items.risk: 21 branches of Mike's own coaching are cut back or withheld before they reach an adviser. The gate is behaving correctly; the content names tools that are not there. Each one is advice an adviser is not getting, and nothing on screen says so.

askedBy.detail: 2026-08-15 — "put them in the list of to dos", after being shown that the seven Seminar branches were seven of twenty-eight. Found by us; filed on his instruction.

items.touches: data/logic_trees.json, the Mentor Hub logic tables, and the Template Check screen where the real page names are settled.
items.note: RANKED LAST DELIBERATELY, and it scores 4. Mike's ruling the same day: clear the technical and feature work first so the master team can start UAT testing, THEN double back to wording and document-title alignment. This is wording and title alignment. The pattern is proven and cheap once a name is known — the Seminar seven took five words and a seven-line diff — but each of the 21 needs the REAL page name, and that is Mike's to give, never a developer's to rule on. Put the actual sentences in front of him, not the label: that is what unblocked 2.3 after four sessions. 🔴 A SECOND STEP WAS FOUND ON 2026-08-26 AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Measuring the empty `templates[]` arrays (raised as 4.51, closed the same day) showed that 22 of the branches with an EMPTY array name their templates in the recommendation PROSE instead — "Use Design & Deliver template", "Use De Bono's 6 Hats" — and those prose names are this item's own missing documents, in the same trees (35, cas_, fbp_). The consequence nobody had recorded: `walkLogicTree` in server/utils/logicTrees.js L1037 reads ONLY `node.templates`, never the prose. So the tree's judgement about which tool fits reaches the ADVISER as a sentence and never reaches the RANKING ENGINE, where it is meant to act as the tie-breaker. When the search content is updated and the names resolve, populating `templates[]` on those 22 branches is a required second step — the sentences alone leave the engine exactly as blind as it is now. ⚠ AND IT CANNOT BE DONE FIRST: `validateLogicTreeReferences` scans `nodes[].templates` and hard-fails under VA_STRICT_CONTENT, so writing a name into the array before the document exists turns a silent gap into a broken build.

Mike says the documents exist and will update the search content, then pick this up. Nothing to do here until he does. MATCHING IGNORES CASE AND PUNCTUATION, so some may already be solved - 'Demings Volatility' is published and matches "Deming's Theory of Volatility"; '6 Hats' matches "De Bono's 6 Hats". A sentence dies if ANY name in it is missing, and four branches name two. 'Psyche Errors' and 'Team AI' may be concepts rather than documents - if so the fix is to reword the sentence and no page is needed. WAS 21, NOW 19: COI Development pt1 and pt2 were published all along and the name scanner was cutting the title at the lowercase 'pt' (fixed in 48265ac). When the search content is updated, re-run the gate over all 55 recommendations - the command is in the reference file. Today: 36 whole / 6 partial / 13 withheld, pinned in tests/unit/recommendationGate.test.js.

items.name: Nobody has seen a real conversation's recommendations reach the Team tab
items.why: Merged 2026-07-22 (PR #21, d791a9a): the AI declares its recommendations in a trailing [[TEMPLATES: ...]] marker that the engine holds back from the stream so it never reaches the advisor. THE LIVE CHECK WAS RUN ON 2026-08-26, on Mike laptop, against a live OpenAI key — three complete client conversations driven through to a Phase 3 recommendation, 17 API calls, 77,605 tokens on gpt-4o-mini. Two of the three checks PASSED and are closed. (a) The reply streams normally: the recommendations arrived in 435, 1,094 and 792 separate chunks, token by token. (b) No marker text is ever visible: not one bracket in 2,321 recorded chunks, tested against every partial prefix of the sentinel, against the chunks joined, and against the final rewritten text — and this is not a vacuous pass, because in the succession run the AI demonstrably DID write a marker (its declared order differs from the deterministic prose-scan order, which only the marker preserves) and not one character of it escaped. What remains is (c) alone.
items.risk: Small, and now smaller than it was: the two checks that could show something ugly on screen have both passed. What is still unseen is whether a real session's recommended templates land correctly on the Team tab and set the right capability tier — the record that decides what an advisor is credited with. It cannot go wrong invisibly forever, but nobody has watched it go right once.

askedBy.detail: Logged at the 2026-07-22 merge as the named residual of that change. Carried in ACTIONS.md until it was frozen 2026-08-24; re-checked 2026-08-26 and still unexercised.

items.touches: nothing — this is a live observation, not a code change. server/utils/activityLogger.js (logVASession) and server/routes/activity.js (/api/activity/team) hold the path if it fails.
items.note: ⚠ ITS ORIGINAL BLOCKER WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL ONE IS DIFFERENT. This item said for a month that it could not be done here because "this machine has no OPENAI_API_KEY and every advisor request fails at startup". That was false: .env on the laptop has held a live key since 30 July, dotenv loads it at server/restify-server.js L50, and the backend logs "[advisor] OPENAI_API_KEY present=true" on boot. The key was never the obstacle. THE REAL OBSTACLE IS MYSQL. The capability record is written by logVASession into the activity store, and on this machine that store logs "database unavailable (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3306) — using the dev file". All three conversations completed and NONE was recorded: the Team tab still reads 2026-08-14 and data/dev-activity.json still ends at 2026-08-10. No error was logged — the write simply did not happen. So (c) needs any environment with a database, which means UAT rather than a developer machine, and it is a two-minute look: open the Team tab as a firm manager after a real session and check the templates and the tier are the ones the conversation actually produced. ⚠ "Team Dashboard", the name this item used to carry, IS NOT A SCREEN — the words appear nowhere in any page or component, only in a JSDoc comment at tierLookup.js L88. The screen is the Team tab, fed by /api/activity/team.
items.comment: 2026-08-26 — checks (a) and (b) run live and passed; see 4.53 for what the same exercise turned up, which is that the AI writes the marker only sometimes and nothing records when it did not.

items.name: The education gate still asks its question, and its documents are gone
items.why: The gate's hub page and all four of its documents were deleted on 2026-08-26 on Mike's instruction, in his words because it is 'a feature we will never use again'. But the question itself still fires: server/advisorEngine.js still asks the advisor, before any recommendation, whether to lead with education or show what is technically needed. So the statement and the code disagree.
items.risk: Live behaviour whose only remaining description is the code itself. An advisor is still asked a question Mike may believe was removed, and nobody reading the documents would know it exists. The reverse risk is real too: removing it touches 15 files and about 1,000 lines, and it is behaviour he ruled on three times.

askedBy.detail: Raised 2026-08-26 by the session that deleted the documents, as the named consequence of deleting them. Nobody outside asked; it is filed because CLAUDE.md requires an open question for Mike to be an item on this list rather than a line in a note.

items.touches: server/utils/educationGate.js, server/advisorEngine.js, data/education-gate.json, data/signal-dictionary.json (gateSignals), tests/unit/educationGate.test.js. Read-only until Mike rules.
items.note: TWO HONEST ANSWERS AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT. (1) Remove the gate entirely — the question stops being asked, about 1,000 lines go, and the deletion of its documents becomes consistent. (2) Keep it — the question is one extra step that cannot change which templates are recommended, and the code plus its test are a sufficient record for something that small. DO NOT DECIDE THIS WITHOUT HIM: he ruled on the behaviour three times (2026-07-16, 2026-08-16, 2026-08-24), and although each was him answering a question we raised, removing shipped behaviour is not a tidy-up.

items.name: The AI declares what it recommended only sometimes, and nothing records when it did not
items.why: Merged 2026-07-22 (PR #21, d791a9a): the AI ends a Phase 3 answer with a trailing [[TEMPLATES: ...]] marker declaring what it actually recommended, so the advisor capability record stops being a guess made by scanning prose. data/prompts/client.txt SECTION 11 instructs it, and that instruction does reach the Phase 3 system prompt (advisorEngine.js L3452 loads the whole file). The first real conversations ever run against it — three of them, on Mike laptop, 2026-08-26, closing 4.50 — show the AI writes the marker only SOMETIMES. In the succession run it wrote one and the hold-back worked perfectly. In the joinery run it wrote none at all, and resolveRecommendedTemplates (tierLookup.js L210) fell through to extractTemplatesFromText — the prose scan the marker was built to replace. The third run genuinely could not be told apart, so the honest count is one confirmed present, one confirmed absent, one unknown; this is NOT a measured rate.
items.risk: The capability record behind the Team Dashboard can be built from prose guesswork with nothing anywhere saying so. That fallback is not a neutral second-best — it is the defect the marker exists to fix. Its own JSDoc records what it did: it missed names the AI had bolded, and it read ordinary sentences such as "your retail shop needs a pivot in leadership" as four recommendations, inflating an advisor recorded tier because Leadership is an advanced-tier tool. Both paths produce a plausible list, so a tester in UAT cannot tell them apart, and nobody can say how often the fallback runs because nothing counts it.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-08-26 by the session running the 4.50 live check — three real conversations against the live OpenAI key on this laptop. Nobody outside asked for it. Filed as a defect with Mike explicit yes when it was put to him. A defect we found ourselves still files; what the gate in tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js bars is a FEATURE nobody asked for.

items.touches: server/advisorEngine.js (the Phase 3 close at L3525, where state.recommendedTemplates is set), server/utils/tierLookup.js (resolveRecommendedTemplates), data/prompts/client.txt SECTION 11.
items.note: THE PROPOSED FIX IS ONE LOG LINE, NOT CHASING THE AI INTO OBEDIENCE. The model ignoring an instruction at the very end of a 15,799-character prompt is not something this repo can reliably fix, and trying would be guesswork. What is missing is that the choice is INVISIBLE: resolveRecommendedTemplates returns a list and never says which of its two paths produced it. Recording declared-vs-prose where state.recommendedTemplates is set turns an unmeasurable coin-toss into a number UAT can watch. ⚠ HOW TO TELL THE TWO APART FROM OUTSIDE, because it is not obvious and it cost this session an hour: (a) the marker preserves the AI OWN order while extractTemplatesFromText always returns catalogue order — so a session_meta order that differs from a fresh prose scan proves a marker was present; (b) stripTemplateMarker right-trims, so a stream ending in an untrimmed blank line proves there was NO marker. Both are readable from the SSE stream alone, with no code change. NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: 5 is arguable rather than 4 if the capability record counts as data integrity — the ranking is Mike.
